StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single with the sim's on_stack overridden to `pass` citing it -- the census's 15-unit wrong-reasoning class (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`). Single means "Amount is hidden and is always 1" (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) and PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally with no StackType branch, so C# really reaches Amount 2. Dormant: nothing reads Imbalanced's Amount on either side (the effect is a boolean off-balance flag), and monsters/hive/bowlbugs.py:47 applies it once at construction.

AfterDamageGiven.issue: WRONG HOOK. C#'s `AfterDamageGiven(choiceContext, dealer, result, props, target, cardSource)` is the DEALER-side after-damage event; the sim's counterpart is `on_damage_dealt` (hooks.py:469, fired at cmds.py:123-124), and this power uses `on_damage_received` instead, filtering on `dealer is self.owner`. The reason the port had to do that is itself the finding: cmds.py:123 fires on_damage_dealt only `if dealer is not None and hp_lost > 0`, so the sim's dealer-side event **cannot see a fully-blocked or zero-damage hit at all**, where C#'s AfterDamageGiven sees every one (`result.WasFullyBlocked` is a field it is expected to read). Consequence of the substitution: cmds.py:121's killing-blow guard suppresses the sim's on_damage_received when the hit killed the VICTIM, and cmds.py:119-120's own comment says "AfterDamageGiven (on_damage_dealt) is not guarded and still fires on the kill" -- so this power silently stops working on a lethal hit in the sim and keeps working in the game. Third-file citations, not hashed here. This unit is the sharpest instance of that shape, because the whole power keys on `result.WasFullyBlocked` (ImbalancedPower.cs:19) -- exactly the case cmds.py:123's `hp_lost > 0` makes invisible to the sim's dealer-side event. The port therefore reads `amount == 0` on the victim's hook (powers.py:2064), which is a BROADER predicate than WasFullyBlocked: hp_lost is 0 for a fully blocked hit, but also for a hit that was 0 to begin with and for one an HP-loss modifier zeroed, neither of which C# calls fully blocked. The sim then narrows it back with an added `ValueProp.MOVE in props` test (powers.py:2065) that C# does NOT have -- recurring gap shape 8 -- so the two predicates differ in both directions. DORMANT: the owner is the Bowlbug Rock (monsters/hive/bowlbugs.py:42-47), whose only damage source is its own HEADBUTT AttackIntent (props MOVE, non-zero), and the player has no ported HP-loss modifier that could zero an enemy's hit -- so the only reachable trigger is a genuine full block, where both predicates agree. Trigger: a 0-damage MOVE from the owner, or any unpowered damage the owner deals. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2067-2071 reproduces both arms with `hasattr(self.owner, "is_off_balance")`, and the sim's docstring says why ("BowlbugRock's move machine reads it"). Faithful, and a good example of a hasattr probe standing in for a C# type test without changing the outcome.

powers.py:2062-2063 tests `dealer is self.owner and target is not self.owner`. The extra `target is not self.owner` clause is the sim's way of not firing on the owner hitting itself, which C# gets for free from being on the dealer-side hook.
